transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-29
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Priya Nair (Redwood AE), Jules Kim (Redwood SRE), Marco Diaz (Redwood CSM); Maya Alvarez (Veridian VP Eng), Tom Becker (Platform Lead), Rohit Singh (SRE), Elena Park (Security)

Summary: Post-incident follow-up — focus on playbook changes to 'heal' SLA during tail latency events, handoff of regression tasks to Veridian ops, and scheduling a lightweight benchmark against a dedicated pool.

Transcript:
[00:00:00] Priya: Okay hey everyone, thanks for joining. we wanted to keep this pretty structured, shortish, 55 minutes ish, go over the healing playbook, handoff, and next steps. Maya, do you want to open with a quick recap from your side?
[00:00:22] Maya: Yeah sure. um thanks Priya. quick recap — last week we saw a tail latency spike during the morning batch window, roughly 10:15 to 10:40, it caused our customer-facing transform pipeline to degrade and we had to fallback to the smaller model. we did the mitigation but want to make sure the fixes are appropriately codified.
[00:00:41] Tom: and just to add -- we saw 99.9 go from 420ms to like 1.8 seconds for roughly 12 minutes, which pushed downstream queues.
[00:00:52] Jules: right, that's consistent with the traces we got from your team — there's a KV cache churn plus a series of long token generation tails when the pool autoscaler spun up new nodes. so it's a combo of cold-kv and model warmup.
[00:01:10] Rohit: and note, the traffic pattern was more bursty than normal, we had a high concurrency burst from a third-party integration at 10:12.
[00:01:18] Priya: cool. goal for this call is agree on the playbook edits — when to fallback, how to adjust batching and TTLs, and who's doing the regression. also confirm the SLA band we shoot for.
[00:01:35] Maya: for us 99.9 under 500ms is the goal, anything above 700ms triggers on-call escalation.
[00:01:45] Priya: noted. Jules, walk us through the playbook changes you propose.
[00:01:51] Jules: yeah. high level: 1) detect: add a short anomaly detector on prefix latency — a sliding window 3 minute median vs 95th baseline, 2) mitigate: immediate soft-fallback policy to a quantized model variant for non-sensitive calls, 3) recover: start a dedicated warmup flow to pre-populate KV cache for predicted hot prefixes, 4) postmortem: collect KV cache key churn slices and full token traces.
[00:02:20] Tom: can you explain the soft-fallback bit — how do we ensure we don't leak PII when moving to a quantized variant?
[00:02:28] Jules: good point, the rule is fallback only for stateless calls or calls that have been flagged as allowed for quantized models. we'll rely on your opt-in header. also the quantized variant respects same inference filters, but we asked to have a redwood-allow-quant header.
[00:02:46] Elena: that opt-in header, do we have an audit trail for it? audits are crucial for us.
[00:02:52] Marco: yes, the playbook will document that every fallback decision is logged as an audit event and surfaced in the console; we can also ship a compressed audit export to S3 on request.
[00:03:05] Maya: would like the audit format to include request id, decision reason, and model variant — that's non-negotiable for compliance.
[00:03:13] Priya: noted, we'll include those fields in the event schema.
[00:03:18] [00:03:30] Priya: next, KV cache changes — Jules?
[00:03:33] Jules: so in the incident we saw TTL collisions — very short TTLs combined with a burst created a churn storm. recommendation: increase prefix cache TTL for ranges with high churn by factor of 2-3 and introduce a leaky-bucket admission to avoid mass evictions on spikes. also add a prewarm step when autoscaler launches new nodes to proactively fetch hot KV entries.
[00:03:59] Tom: how intrusive is the prewarm? will it add time to node boot?
[00:04:05] Jules: marginal; it's background async fetches for top N prefixes from recent telemetry. should not block the node from accepting traffic but will reduce cold misses in first 30s.
[00:04:16] Rohit: do we have telemetry for top prefixes? we didn't send the full prefix list last time.
[00:04:21] Marco: that's on us — we asked for a lighter telemetry hook, we'll provide a secure stream (redacted prefixes) so you can opt-in; we'll include sampling to limit volume.
[00:04:34] Maya: we need to keep data residency rules in mind when streaming prefix telemetry.
[00:04:38] Elena: specifically, prefix sampling must strip any PII and be encrypted in transit and at rest; KMS keys must be customer-managed if possible.
[00:04:47] Jules: agreed. playbook will flag telemetry endpoints that require CMK usage.
[00:04:53] [00:05:10] Priya: on the SLA thresholds — Maya sets 99.9 under 500ms, escalation at 700ms. any objections?
[00:05:16] Tom: sounds reasonable but we should allow a brief warmup window after releases.
[00:05:21] Priya: we'll add release windows as exceptions — 10 minute golden window where we expect slight variance.
[00:05:28] Maya: okay.
[00:05:33] [00:06:00] Priya: rolling back to the regression handoff: we want to hand the raw traces and a short checklist to your ops for the regression tickets. Jules, what do you need to deliver?
[00:06:09] Jules: I'll deliver: 1) KV-cache churn slices with timestamps and affected prefixes, 2) model invocation traces (token timing and sequence length), 3) autoscaler events correlated to node boots, and 4) suggested TTL and admission changes.
[00:06:25] Maya: timeline?
[00:06:27] Jules: aiming to drop that to you by 2026-02-06, that's what we put in the action items.
[00:06:33] Tom: and we will schedule a 60-minute run against a small dedicated test pool to validate the change, proposed date 2026-02-05.
[00:06:42] Priya: great. Marco, what's in the playbook doc share?
[00:06:46] Marco: the share will include a step-by-step pain tree, exact CLI commands for toggles, a sample audit-export link, and a decision matrix for fallback vs degrade. we'll also include an appendix for SSO and KMS config.
[00:06:59] Elena: can you include the list of RBAC roles that will read audit logs? security needs to approve.
[00:07:05] Marco: yes.
[00:07:10] [00:07:40] Rohit: quick question — during the incident, we had a small number of 403s to the KMS endpoint, I suspect transient auth token expiry. did you see anything?
[00:07:51] Jules: I saw a handful of short-lived KMS timeouts; we did surface an alert to the console. not a systemic KMS failure. could be a regional network blip.
[00:08:00] Tom: if KMS goes flaky, do we have fallback to cached KEKs?
[00:08:06] Marco: we generally do not recommend cached keys for customer-managed keys, but there is a read-only cached envelope that can be used for unsealed sessions in emergencies — documented in the recovery appendix.
[00:08:20] Elena: we need a clear policy on that; we'll review the appendix.
[00:08:25] [00:08:50] Priya: switching to measure/benchmark — we want to run the same load profile against a small dedicated pool. questions: what tool, how long, and what telemetry do we need?
[00:08:59] Tom: we can run k6 or our in-house harness. prefer reproducible at 1.2x normal burst.
[00:09:05] Jules: we can run Redwood benchmark harness, we recommend 10 minutes steady + 5 minute burst and capture token-level traces + KV cache hit rates.
[00:09:15] Maya: 10+5 sounds fine. please make sure the harness includes realistic sequence length distribution, we had longer conversations in the morning.
[00:09:23] Priya: Jules will produce the harness config and we'll share as a gist.
[00:09:28] [00:09:50] Priya: ok next — communications plan for customers during any mitigation. Maya, legal/regulatory constraints?
[00:09:57] Maya: must include a ticket in our system with classification and a weekly summary for audit. cannot send raw traces outside org without redaction.
[00:10:06] Marco: understood — we'll only send redacted traces and a replay bundle with request ids.
[00:10:12] Elena: encryption in transit & at rest is mandatory for any bundle.
[00:10:16] Priya: point well taken. we'll include encryption and CMK notes in the playbook.
[00:10:22] [00:10:45] Priya: anything from compliance or legal that blocks the mitigation?
[00:10:51] Elena: just the trace redaction and CMK requirement; otherwise fine.
[00:10:55] [00:11:20] Priya: open items recap: we'll edit playbook for TTL/admission changes, add fallback audit schema, provide prewarm guidance, and produce traces. agreed?
[00:11:28] Maya: yes.
[00:11:34] Tom: yes.
[00:11:36] [00:11:52] Priya: timeline recap: playbook share 2026-02-02, benchmark 2026-02-05, traces 2026-02-06, canary window 2026-02-09 if all good.
[00:12:04] Maya: tentative canary on the 9th works for us.
[00:12:09] Priya: ok. any last risks we should call out?
[00:12:15] Jules: risk — if prefix telemetry can't be shared due to residency, prewarm effectiveness reduces. mitigation: use local prewarm config on customer side and share only metrics.
[00:12:28] Elena: we'll validate residency with legal today.
[00:12:33] [00:12:50] Priya: good. one more thing — competitors mentioned. Maya earlier asked if fallback would route to alternate vendor; any appetite?
[00:12:58] Maya: we tested a multi-vendor fallback in the past but prefer single vendor due to consistency.
[00:13:05] Priya: ok noted.
[00:13:15] [00:13:40] Marco: i'll put links in chat: playbook draft (link), sample audit export (s3 link placeholder), and benchmark config gist.
[00:13:49] [00:14:10] Priya: excellent. let's capture final agreed action items.
[00:14:15] Marco: action items are in the notes, will send a calendar invite for the benchmark window and the regression handoff meeting.
[00:14:22] Maya: thanks all.
[00:14:25] Priya: thanks everyone. meeting adjourned.
